title: Lessons from Trillion Token Deployments at Fortune 500s — Alessandro Cappelli, Adaptive ML
talk_summary: The talk argues that RL-style feedback loops, not one-off prompting or SFT, are how enterprises systematically improve models in production. The transferable mechanisms are reward signals from executable checks, human-defined rubrics for LLM judges, mock environments, and rejection-sampled trajectories for evals.

takeaways.what_they_do: They prefer systematic reward signals such as whether code runs or syntax is correct, and use LLM judges only for open-ended criteria like tone or business rules.
takeaways.evidence_quote: does the code run? Is the syntax is correct?

takeaways.what_they_do: Humans define rubrics, judge system prompts, and scenarios rather than running expensive annotation campaigns; LLM judges then score open-ended behavior.
takeaways.evidence_quote: the human in the loop is helping just by defining the rubrics, defining the system prompt to these LLMs judges

takeaways.what_they_do: Once an environment and reward exist, they generate agent trajectories and keep the ones the reward marks as good, creating a synthetic eval/training data pipeline.
takeaways.evidence_quote: you can literally create trajectories that are good because the reward that you put in place will tell you what is good

takeaways.technique: Mock tools and mock users for agent evals
takeaways.what_they_do: If a real environment is unavailable, they mock tools and even a mock user LLM so agents can be trained/evaluated against realistic scenarios.
takeaways.evidence_quote: you can still mock the tools and you can mock, if you need one for the specific case, a mock user

takeaways.technique: Smaller models for narrow high-volume tasks
takeaways.what_they_do: They argue RL-specialized smaller models can match larger-model performance on narrow tasks while being cheaper and faster to serve.
takeaways.evidence_quote: those models will be cheaper to serve at scale
takeaways.numbers: agents can use 10x more tokens than simple summarization; half-second latency is already awkward for speech

takeaways.what_they_do: They start with a prompted large LLM judge, then use accumulated production feedback to train reward models and scale human feedback.
takeaways.evidence_quote: we use this data to train reward models
